question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><mover><mi>r</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>·</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mover><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> be a plane. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> be another plane which passes through the points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>. If the direction ratios of the line of intersection of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>16</mn></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></math> is equal to ______.

solution.text:
Given P1:r→·2i^+j^-3k^=4

i.e. P1:2x+y-3z=4

Equation of P2 is given by x-2y+3z-201-5-1-10=0

⇒-5x+5y+z+23=0

Now n1→×n2→=i^j^k^21-3-551=16i^+13j^+15k^

Let a,b,c be the DR's of the line of intersection

Then a=16λ15;b=13λ15;c=15λ15

∴α=13:β=15

Hence α+β=28
